front: How does Shakespeare present Macbeth’s ambition in the play as a whole?
back: Model: Macbeth’s desire for power leads him to murder Duncan. Marking points: support a developed interpretation and analyse Shakespeare’s methods. Trap: retelling the plot.
subdeck_path: Eduqas GCSE English Literature C720QS – Exam technique::Assessment skills::Assessment skills:: Assessment skills

front: How does the writer present responsibility in An Inspector Calls?
back: Model: Sheila accepts responsibility for her treatment of Eva. Marking points: use the extract and whole play; analyse dramatic methods. Trap: ignoring the extract.
subdeck_path: Eduqas GCSE English Literature C720QS – Exam technique::Assessment skills::Assessment skills:: Assessment skills

front: How does Dickens present Scrooge’s transformation in A Christmas Carol?
back: Model: Scrooge’s generosity at the end reverses his earlier selfishness. Marking points: support a reading across the novel and analyse methods in context. Trap: recounting events alone.
subdeck_path: Eduqas GCSE English Literature C720QS – Exam technique::Assessment skills::Assessment skills:: Assessment skills

front: How does Blake present education in The Schoolboy?
back: Model: Blake contrasts the child’s pleasure outdoors with the misery he associates with school. Marking points: support an interpretation with textual detail and analyse language or structure. Trap: retell the poem without explaining effects.
subdeck_path: Eduqas GCSE English Literature C720QS – Exam technique::Assessment skills::Assessment skills:: Assessment skills

front: Compare experiences of war in Disabled and Drummer Hodge.
back: Model: Owen depicts a veteran’s continuing isolation, while Hardy presents a young soldier buried far from home. Marking points: analyse methods in both poems, compare interpretations and relate relevant context. Trap: discuss only one poem.
subdeck_path: Eduqas GCSE English Literature C720QS – Exam technique::Assessment skills::Assessment skills:: Assessment skills

front: How does Shakespeare use Lady Macbeth’s sleepwalking to present guilt?
back: Model: Her attempt to clean an imagined stain suggests that the murder continues to trouble her. Marking points: support a focused interpretation and analyse dramatic methods. Trap: describe the murder without analysing the scene.
subdeck_path: Eduqas GCSE English Literature C720QS – Exam technique::Assessment skills::Assessment skills:: Assessment skills

front: Compare how The Schoolboy and I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud present nature.
back: Model: Blake contrasts natural freedom with school, while Wordsworth shows remembered flowers restoring pleasure. Marking points: compare supported interpretations and analyse each poet’s methods and relevant context. Trap: write separate summaries without comparison.
